fields.sample_size: 506 households in 25 water supply schemes (about 21 per scheme; old and new schemes and deep tube-well schemes) in three distribution zones (near the reservoir, mid-distribution, tail end) selected by purposive sampling; household survey 2022-2024 with a structured schedule; secondary data on 135 water plants, capacities and production from city institutions; GIS and Google Earth mapping
fields.effect_measure: descriptive tabulation (Excel) of household water obtained per week, litres, hours and frequency of supply by zone and scheme; GIS mapping; no inferential statistics
fields.effect_estimate: Only 34% of the city population has access to the urban water system although 135 water plants operate; plants produce below designed capacity because they are old (more than 30 years); cracks and leakages cause suspension of supply and contamination, and illegal connections reduce pressure for neighbours; a May 2023 pipeline burst killed two people and injured about 30. Households at the tail end of the distribution system obtain less water for fewer hours than households near reservoirs (zone comparisons in the tables), and more than 65% of residents depend on groundwater. The authors conclude that the system has low accessibility, poor quality and compromised reliability and that the city corporation gives the water supply system little priority; they propose decentralising the supply network.
fields.section: Full text (13 pages): Introduction; Materials and methods; Results (infrastructure, ageing, leakage, water theft, household water security by zone); Conclusion
fields.exact_location: Materials and methods (506 households, 25 schemes); Table 1 (plant production); results on illegal connections and zone differences; Visnyk Karazin Univ. Series Geology Geography Ecology 61:377-391

evidence_level: Single-study evidence: a descriptive household survey (506 households, three distribution zones) and GIS study of water security and infrastructure in Guwahati; read in full text 2026-10-04. Descriptive only; the institutional element is limited to remarks on water theft, city-corporation priority and decentralisation.
